UPSC Photo and Signature Size

UPSC application and registration screens set ranges for the photograph and signature images. Use these presets and then confirm the numbers against the instructions on the portal.

Quick answer: UPSC guidance commonly describes a photo and a signature image in JPG within KB ranges and pixel limits. Use the matching preset, compress, check the minimum as well as the maximum, and verify on the official portal.

Size ranges last reviewed: 2026-10-04. Always confirm against your exam notification.

Free image compression tool

Target size Target size:
Exam range: Targets sit a little below the maximum. Check your notice.
Advanced settings

By default the tool keeps quality reasonable (about 62% or higher) and reduces dimensions to reach small targets; tick “Keep dimensions” to prefer full size at lower quality. Aspect ratio is always preserved and images are never enlarged. PNG is lossless and may not reach a small target; JPEG/WebP are lossy. JPEG replaces transparency with white; WebP and PNG keep it.

What UPSC asks for

Requirements change with every notification. The ranges on this page are figures commonly reported for recent 2026 notices by exam-preparation websites, and the sources do not always agree. We have not verified them against each official PDF, so always follow the notification or instructions on the official application portal for your exam.

Reports of recent UPSC guidance describe a colour passport-size photograph in JPG format of roughly 20–200 KB, and a signature image of roughly 20–100 KB with a width of about 350–500 pixels. One source quotes up to 300 KB for the photograph, which shows how figures vary.

Reports also mention live photograph capture and a signature image that contains three signatures in black ink.

Photograph preparation

Use a recent, clear colour photograph with a plain background and your face filling most of the frame, as the instructions describe. Crop to the required shape first, then use the Photo 20–200 KB preset here. The target of 190 KB leaves a margin under 200 KB.

Signature preparation

If your instructions ask for several signatures in one image, sign with a dark pen on plain white paper, leave space between the signatures, and photograph the sheet evenly. Crop around them and run the Signature 20–100 KB preset. The result card shows size and dimensions so you can compare them to the stated width range.

File names and format

Some instructions ask you to name files in a particular way. Rename the downloaded file after compression, and make sure the extension matches the real format. Renaming a PNG to .jpg does not convert it; use JPEG output here so the file is genuinely a JPEG.

Minimum size

UPSC ranges have a minimum as well as a maximum. A very simple image can fall under the minimum even at high quality. The tool will show a warning if that happens. In that case, use a higher-resolution original or keep more of the surrounding paper in the crop.

Keep one consistent signature

Your uploaded signature may be compared with what you sign later in the process. Practise the style you upload and use it consistently, as the official instructions advise.

Quick checklist

Confirm the current range on the portal, crop the photograph to the required shape, prepare the signature sheet on plain white paper, compress each file with its own preset, check the minimum as well as the maximum, name the files as instructed, and save a copy of everything you submit.

Because live photograph matching may be part of the process, use a recent photograph that looks like you now, taken in good light, and avoid heavy filters or editing of the face.

UPSC Civil Services, NDA, and CDS photo and signature specifications

The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) enforces rigorous digital image guidelines for Civil Services (CSE), NDA, CDS, and Engineering Services applications. Official notifications consistently specify a file size range of 20KB to 300KB for candidate photographs and 20KB to 300KB for signatures, with explicit pixel dimension requirements (such as 350×350 to 1000×1000 pixels).

To prepare your UPSC application assets: ensure your photo is recent with a clear front-facing pose occupying at least three-quarters of the frame. When preparing signatures, ensure the file stays above the 20KB minimum floor. You can use our custom size box to compress image to 20KB or target 40KB to 50KB for outstanding clarity that easily satisfies UPSC portal validation.

UPSC One Time Registration (OTR) profile photo updates

Candidates maintaining an active profile on the UPSC One Time Registration (OTR) portal must periodically update their photo and signature to reflect their current likeness. Our client-side compressor processes your documents locally in your browser, ensuring absolute privacy when updating your permanent UPSC credentials.

UPSC dimensional parameters: pixel aspect ratio and framing rules

The Union Public Service Commission portal enforces strict dimensional constraints alongside file size limits. For Civil Services and combined examinations, candidate photographs must fall between 350×350 and 1000×1000 pixels, maintaining a square or near-square aspect ratio where the candidate face covers at least 75% of the total frame.

Similarly, candidate signatures must fall within 350×350 to 1000×1000 pixels. To satisfy both dimensional bounding boxes and file size ceilings (20KB to 300KB), set maximum dimensions to 600×600 pixels in our Advanced settings. This keeps your photo beautifully sharp, prevents pixelation during admit card generation, and ensures immediate compliance with UPSC automated validation scripts.

Name and date imprint requirements for UPSC candidate photographs

Recent UPSC notifications mandate that candidate photographs must not be more than 10 days old from the start of the online application process, and should clearly display the candidate name and the date of photograph capture at the bottom of the image.

When adding text imprints to your photo, ensure the font is legible and does not obscure the chin or neck. Our tool compresses the final composite without blurring the printed date or name.

Common questions

Is it 200 KB or 300 KB for the photo?

Sources differ and it can change by notice. Read the limit on the upload screen. If unsure, stay well under the lower figure.

Does this tool create three signatures in one image?

No. It only compresses and resizes an image you provide. Prepare the signatures on paper first, then photograph the whole sheet and crop it before compressing.

What if my signature file is under 20 KB?

Then it is below the usual minimum for this range. Photograph the sheet larger or sharper, crop with a little more margin, and run it again.
